newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton rises, helped by credit availability.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton rises, helped by credit availability.

text.p: Indian cotton prices gained on Wednesday on reduced arrivals and easier availability of credit, dealers said.
They said the market was buoyant following a government move at the weekend to lift credit controls on cotton and some other commodities.

New crop arrivals fell owing to unseasonal rains in producing areas. Traders said higher arrivals were due next month. In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees to 1,010/1,060 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and Gujarat Sankar-4 by 100 to 20,600/21,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
